common_name: Enduring Summer White Crapemyrtle (True Dwarf Reblooming Disease-Resistant Series)

planting.note: Set out container plants in late winter through fall in well-drained soil and full sun; this true-dwarf selection in the Enduring Summer line stays a tidy 4-5 feet, giving a white-flowered option where the larger tree-form crapemyrtles would overwhelm a small bed or patio planter.

directions: Site in full sun and well-drained, moderately fertile soil; the compact mounded habit of this white-flowered Enduring Summer selection suits foundation plantings, mixed borders, or large patio containers far better than a standard tree-form crapemyrtle would. Breeding for leaf-spot and powdery mildew resistance keeps foliage cleaner through humid summers, and removing spent flower clusters encourages the next flush of white blooms. Limit pruning to removing dead, damaged, or crossing stems in late winter, since this series flowers on both old and new wood and does not need the hard cutback some older crapemyrtles are given.

common_name: Enduring Summer Pink Crapemyrtle (True Dwarf Reblooming Disease-Resistant Series)

planting.note: Install container-grown plants in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this rich-pink member of the Enduring Summer series holds to a compact 4-5 feet, making it a fit for small-space landscapes where a full-size crapemyrtle tree would not.

directions: Grow in full sun and well-drained soil of average fertility; large pink flower trusses are produced non-stop from early summer into fall, with the heaviest flush of rebloom coming after spent clusters are deadheaded. This true-dwarf habit avoids the need for size-control pruning that taller crapemyrtle cultivars require, so routine maintenance is limited to clearing out dead or crowded interior twigs in late winter. Leaf-spot and powdery mildew resistance bred into the series keeps the dark green foliage attractive through the humid part of the growing season.

common_name: Enduring Summer Fuchsia Crapemyrtle (True Dwarf Reblooming Disease-Resistant Series)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in late winter through fall in well-drained soil in full sun; the vivid purple-pink flowers of this Enduring Summer selection sit on a true-dwarf 4-6 foot frame, small enough for mixed shrub borders or large mixed containers.

directions: Plant in full sun and well-drained soil; the vibrant fuchsia-pink blooms appear from early summer through early fall and intensify with regular deadheading of spent flower heads. Heat and drought tolerance once established make this a low-maintenance choice for Gulf South and similar hot-summer climates. Prune only to remove dead, damaged, or crossing wood in late winter, since the compact dwarf habit of this series eliminates the need for size-reduction cuts that larger crapemyrtle cultivars often receive.

common_name: Enduring Summer Lavender Crapemyrtle (True Dwarf Reblooming Disease-Resistant Series)

planting.note: Set container plants out in late winter, spring, or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this lavender-flowered Enduring Summer selection keeps to a compact 4-5 foot frame, giving a soft purple color option in a footprint small enough for foundation beds or large containers.

directions: Site in full sun with well-drained soil of average fertility; soft lavender flower clusters open from early summer and continue in flushes into fall, especially where faded trusses are removed promptly. Foliage emerges with a reddish tinge before maturing to dark green, adding seasonal interest beyond the bloom period. Because this series was bred for leaf-spot and powdery mildew resistance, routine care is mostly limited to a light late-winter cleanup of dead or crossing stems rather than disease management or hard pruning for size control.
